rationale: B wins because it finds the missing buyer-side story: "Three insurers just bet that 25 million members will meditate on the plan's dime" gives a reporter a protagonist and a purchasing decision, not just Calm's announcement. A is strong, especially "A Calm-funded trial reports an 18% drop in anxiety — the question is whether 'regular users' is doing the heavy lifting," but it leaves the insurer rationale mostly folded into a broader category trend. B also asks the nastier proof question: whether the 18% is "a between-group difference or a within-group change." That's the kind of line that keeps a founder from walking into a science reporter's blender.
gaps_in_A: "Wellness apps are crossing from app-store impulse buy into reimbursed health benefit" risks making a trend out of one data point; A knows this and caveats it, but the headline still overstates what the supplied facts prove.
"a company with 4M+ paying subscribers is now handing the product away free" is a little too cute unless Calm's payment structure confirms this is not just insurer-paid access.
A misses a clean insurer-protagonist angle. The payer decision is the second-most-reportable thing here, and A mostly treats payers as context for Calm or the category.
"AI-slop/sponsored-research skepticism journalists are writing about right now" imports a zeitgeist peg the update did not supply. Small line, but still an invented gloss.
gaps_in_B: "at a moment when demand for care exceeds clinician supply" is invented from outside the update. Maybe true, maybe not; either way, it is not in the packet.
"category-creation" is a grandiose story-type label for a one-company, three-insurer deal. The proof section wisely says not to claim first, but the label is still wearing a press-release hat.
"meditate on the plan's dime" is punchy, but it can sound flippant for a mental-health coverage story. Use it internally, not in the pitch subject line.
The category and insurer angles overlap around payer coverage; they are distinct enough to keep, but they need sharply different media lists or they become the same pitch with different shoes.
